How to Read a Colorado Well Permit

Buying rural land in Colorado? If the property has a well—or you plan to drill one—it’s essential to understand what the well permit says. Here's a simple guide to decoding it.

Where to Find the Permit

Colorado well permits are issued by the Colorado Division of Water Resources (DWR). You can request a copy or search by address or parcel number in the DWR well permit database.

Key Items on the Permit

  • Permit number – Unique to each well
  • Well location – Township, range, section coordinates
  • Type of use – Household-use only, domestic, irrigation, etc.
  • Depth – Total depth of the well in feet
  • Yield (GPM) – Gallons per minute of output
  • Construction log – Soil layers, casing size, screen depth

Household-Use Only vs. Domestic

  • Household-use only: Water can be used indoors only (no irrigation, no animals)
  • Domestic use: May allow limited irrigation and livestock watering—read the permit closely
A common misconception is that all wells allow outdoor use. In Colorado, many only support indoor household use unless upgraded.

Why It Matters

  • Resale value depends on usable water access
  • Loan approval may require sufficient water rights
  • You may not be able to garden, irrigate, or run a greenhouse without a proper permit

  • Colorado Well Permit Info
